prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Sentinel Vale: EO mission ground segment (plan, acquire, operate, produce, archive, access control; excludes spacecraft, launch, user processing); security: least privilege, strong auth, segmentation, audit. Mission Control Center (Bluebell): real-time ops, anomaly response, releases validated commands, owns contact schedule/routing policy; time-limited elevated access with approved shift role; declares continuity modes (objective, duration, exit criteria); sends constraints to Mission Planning System (MPS), receives command preparation package; demonstrates continuous console coverage, complete handover logs. MPS uses Laser Retroreflector Window; applies Ephemeris Delta Note in schedule validation. Spacecraft Operations Team (SOT): console lead declares pass status, authorizes commands, pauses on telemetry mismatch; uses Antenna Deicing Notice, Pass Replay Packet; receives maneuver recommendation package; day-in-the-life rehearsal. Escalation console>discipline lead>mission management. Stack queued only with MCC+SOT concurrence. Command Validation Gateway (Osprey): shall validate stacks, reject unapproved edits/missing provenance/expired config/out-of-window/missing authorization, validation result, operator acknowledgment; accepts Star Tracker Mask File from Flight Dynamics Facility (Mistral) only if matching security baseline; consults Telemetry Ingest Service, Orbit Determination Engine. Mistral sends ephemerides to MCC, MPS, PPF. Cybersecurity Desk: receives Security Exception Ticket from Ground Network Manager (Juniper); validates alert routing, privileged access, incident coordination. Juniper coordinates cross-site failover; accepts antenna baseline only with current maintenance clearances for North S-Band, South S-Band, Kiruna X-Band, Svalbard X-Band Antennas. Network Control System (Lantern): enforces routing, sends MCC antenna status, link config; records outage rehearsals. Flight Dynamics Team: Doppler Residual Report, Ephemeris Delta Note; degraded-data rehearsal. Payload Calibration Team: Calibration Patch Bundle. Product Quality Service: Product Hold List to User Services Portal (blocks release until cleared; no speculative cause before incident lead approval). Payload Processing Facility (Forgehouse): quarantine unproven lineage; Primary Processing Cluster pauses nonessential queues; Backup Processing Cluster transfer after custody/baseline/authorization verified, uses Storage Watermark Snapshot for capacity. Long Term Archive (Granite): custody reference, Storage Watermark Snapshot; reconcile delayed ingest; retrieval tests before stable. Cedar suspends schedule publication on anomaly. New part:
S244: Operational key performance indicators include contact success rate, telemetry completeness, command validation timeliness, product latency, product quality disposition time, archive availability, help desk responsiveness, and unresolved anomaly age.
S245: Each key performance indicator has an assigned data source, sampling interval, review owner, threshold, and corrective action trigger so that routine reporting does not depend on informal judgment.
S246: The primary monthly service review compares actual performance against the accepted baseline and records trend explanations for any measure that moves outside the watch band.
S247: The Primary Processing Cluster and Backup Processing Cluster are baselined with approved software versions, processing configurations, capacity reservations, monitoring checks, and rollback instructions before handover.
S248: Configuration baselines for ground software, operational procedures, interface control data, account roles, and monitoring rules are frozen at readiness review entry and changed only through approved change control.
S249: Handover to routine mission service is authorized when acceptance evidence is complete, rehearsals meet their objectives, open risks are acknowledged by accountable owners, and support teams confirm on-call coverage.
S250: After handover, the first operational reporting cycle is treated as a stabilization period in which deviations are reviewed daily and permanent process changes are deferred until sufficient evidence is available.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
